article_title: Typology of Generative AI Tools for Education
citation: Matt Bower, Jodie Torrington, Jennifer W. M. Lai. (2026). 2026 Typology of Generative AI Tools for Education. https://bit.ly/2026GenAITypologyData
title: 2026 GenAI Typology survey dataset of educator tool usage
description: The dataset underlying the typology comes from a Generative AI Pedagogies and Technologies Questionnaire distributed internationally, predominantly via professional education networks on LinkedIn and Facebook. Educators nominated specific tools they used within each of the nine categories, with an Other Miscellaneous category capturing tools that did not fit. The article states: "The dataset can be found at https://bit.ly/2026GenAITypologyData" and reports 211 completed responses from educators in 9 countries across elementary school, high school and higher education.
requirements: Publicly available at the printed link
constraints: Responses collected in late 2025; represents a single point-in-time snapshot
target_learners: educators from nine countries spanning early childhood through higher education
target_learning_goals: identifying frequently used generative AI tools in educational practice
examples: Only tools with a frequency greater than 1, meaning used by two or more educators, were included in the final typology
key_sources: Matt Bower, Jodie Torrington, Jennifer W. M. Lai. (2026). 2026 Typology of Generative AI Tools for Education. https://bit.ly/2026GenAITypologyData

article_title: A study of the relationship between institutional policy, organisational culture and e-learning use in four South African universities
citation: Czerniewicz, L. & Brown, C. (2009). A study of the relationship between institutional policy, organisational culture and elearning use in four South African universities. Computers & Education, 53, 121-131. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2009.01.006
title: 2007 South African ICT access and use survey with 26 ICT-mediated activities categorised by Laurillard's Conversational Framework
description: A questionnaire survey of ICT access and use in six diverse South African universities, comprising access, use and demographics parts. Use was categorised into "26 ICT - mediated activities in four of the media form groupings in Laurillard's Conversational Framework (2002)", linking ICT use to the teaching and learning events of acquisition, discovery, dialogue, practice and creation. Respondents reported courses using ICTs, frequency of use for the 26 activities, and satisfaction with management, technical and pedagogical support.
requirements: Print surveys handed out on campus, as online response was very poor
constraints: Realised response rates were 27% for students (3533 usable responses) and 16% for staff (216 usable responses); representativeness of respondent views cannot be known and smaller campuses were under-represented
target_learning_goals: measuring ICT use for teaching and learning across communicative, interactive, adaptive and productive media forms
examples: The four-institution subset analysed here comprised 101/760, 34/296, 21/564 and 36/419 staff/student respondents respectively

article_title: Learning outcomes for communication skills across the health professions: a systematic literature review and qualitative synthesis.
citation: Denniston C, Molloy E, Nestel D, Woodward-Kron R, Keating JL. (2017). Learning outcomes for communication skills across the health professions: a systematic literature review and qualitative synthesis. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2016-014570
title: Final synthesised list of 205 communication skills learning outcomes (online supplementary appendix C)
description: The review's released artifact is a refined set of 205 learning outcomes for communication skills education, presented in the four domains of knowledge, content, process and perceptual skills, and published in online supplementary appendix C. The article states the list "covers a wide range of skills proposed for communication teaching" and provides educators and learners with a comprehensive set for educational design and goal setting in healthcare communication. Outcomes were refined to be concise, defined and accessible to educators developing individualised education programmes.
requirements: Educators are invited to reinterpret the outcomes based on their context, aligned with the social constructionist perspective
constraints: The results do not include input from other key stakeholders such as care seekers, learners and educators, so the authors do not claim it is a complete list illustrative of all stakeholders' needs
target_learners: health professional learners across professions and levels of education
target_learning_goals: communication skills learning goals for educational design and goal setting in healthcare communication
examples: Content-domain outcomes are presented in the chronological sequence of a healthcare interaction
key_sources: Denniston C, Molloy E, Nestel D, Woodward-Kron R, Keating JL. (2017). Learning outcomes for communication skills across the health professions: a systematic literature review and qualitative synthesis. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2016-014570

article_title: Comparing hybrid problem-based and lecture learning (PBL + LBL) with LBL pedagogy on clinical curriculum learning for medical students in China: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
citation: Liu CX, Ouyang WW, Wang XW, Chen D, Jiang ZL. (2020). Comparing hybrid problem-based and lecture learning (PBL + LBL) with LBL pedagogy on clinical curriculum learning for medical students in China: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000019687
title: Evidence base of 20 Chinese RCTs comparing PBL+LBL with LBL across specialized clinical courses
description: The meta-analysis's evidence base consists of 20 randomized controlled studies, all from China, identified from 126 records screened to 34 and finally included after full-text review. It involves "a total of 1817 students, including 910 students in PBL+LBL group and 907 group in LBL group". Courses span gynecology and obstetrics, hepatobiliary surgery, cardiothoracic surgery, dermatology, breast surgery, vascular surgery, general practice, internal medicine, general surgery, infectious diseases, and pediatrics. Study quality was assessed with Cochrane Collaboration's risk-of-bias tool.
requirements: Studies had to be randomized controlled comparisons with PBL+LBL as experimental group and LBL as control group in specialized clinical courses, with sample size at least 10
constraints: All included studies were from China and published in Chinese, limiting generalizability as the authors state
target_learners: clinical medicine students in Chinese medical education
target_learning_goals: clinical theoretical knowledge, clinical skills, medical record writing, comprehensive ability
examples: The search covered PubMed, EBSCO, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Wanfang, CNKI, and CBM up to June 2019
key_sources: Liu CX, Ouyang WW, Wang XW, Chen D, Jiang ZL. (2020). Comparing hybrid problem-based and lecture learning (PBL + LBL) with LBL pedagogy on clinical curriculum learning for medical students in China: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000019687

article_title: Short-Term and Long-Term Retention of Vocabulary through Authentic Subtitled Videos
citation: Nader Asadi Aidinlou & Alireza Moradinejad. (2016). Short-term and Long-term Retention of Vocabulary through Authentic Subtitled Videos. Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.7n.5p.14
title: 20-item multiple-choice vocabulary retention test (KR-21 = 0.89)
description: The study measured vocabulary retention with a researcher-constructed test: "a test o f vocabulary with 20 items was constructed", administered as a multiple-choice paper-pencil test. Reliability was estimated with the Kuder-Richardson formula (KR-21), yielding 0.89, which the authors interpret as reliable. The same test in a different version was used for the delayed post-test, with 20-minute sessions and no penalty for guessing.
requirements: Administered identically at both time points (a different version of the same test for the delayed administration)
target_learners: advanced EFL learners in a vocabulary course
target_learning_goals: measuring short-term and long-term vocabulary retention
examples: Post-test and delayed post-test administrations separated by three weeks, each lasting 20 minutes
key_sources: Nader Asadi Aidinlou & Alireza Moradinejad. (2016). Short-term and Long-term Retention of Vocabulary through Authentic Subtitled Videos. Advances in Language and Literary Studies. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.7n.5p.14

article_title: Knowledge-based Basic Life Support competency and associated factors among healthcare professionals across different hospital levels: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
citation: Pan Pan, Zhou YaXiong, Jiang YaoWen, Xia YiQin, Han TianYong, Pan E., Chen Yao. (2026). Knowledge-based Basic Life Support competency and associated factors among healthcare professionals across different hospital levels: a multicenter cross-sectional study. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1881120
title: 20-item electronic BLS knowledge questionnaire developed with reference to 2020 AHA and 2021 ERC guidelines.
description: The research team developed an electronic questionnaire with reference to the 2020 American Heart Association Guidelines and the 2021 European Resuscitation Council Guidelines for Basic Life Support. It comprised '20 knowledge items' covering core CPR procedures, airway management, defibrillation-related knowledge, and resuscitation quality-control principles. Each correct answer received 5 points, giving a total score between 0 and 100. Cronbach's alpha was 0.701, indicating acceptable internal consistency.
requirements: The questionnaire was developed with reference to international BLS guidelines available during questionnaire development and survey administration
constraints: The article states the questionnaire 'did not undergo formal external content validation or independent pilot testing' and no Content Validity Index or Ratio was calculated
target_learners: Healthcare professionals including physicians, nurses, technicians, and other clinical staff
examples: High knowledge-based BLS competency was determined as a score of ≥80 points, corresponding to at least 16 correct responses out of 20 items
key_sources: Pan Pan, Zhou YaXiong, Jiang YaoWen, Xia YiQin, Han TianYong, Pan E., Chen Yao. (2026). Knowledge-based Basic Life Support competency and associated factors among healthcare professionals across different hospital levels: a multicenter cross-sectional study. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1881120

article_title: Comparison of ChatGPT and DeepSeek on a Standardized Audiologist Qualification Examination in Chinese: Observational Study.
citation: Mavragani A, Hu J, Balogun Oluwadotun C, Qi B, Zheng Y, Wang Y, Xu L. (2025). Comparison of ChatGPT and DeepSeek on a Standardized Audiologist Qualification Examination in Chinese: Observational Study. JMIR Formative Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/79534
title: 2024 Taiwan Audiologist Qualification Examination (TAQE) as a Chinese-language audiology benchmark
description: The 2024 TAQE is a professional licensing examination for audiologists written in traditional Chinese, comprising "300 multiple-choice questions across 6 subject areas" with 50 questions per area. In this study the officially released questions and answer sheets were downloaded as a PDF, entered manually into the models' dialogue interfaces with a fixed prompt, and used to benchmark GPT-4-turbo and DeepSeek-R1 by overall accuracy, subject-specific scores, and question-type scores.
requirements: Questions and options must be entered into the model dialogue interface with a fixed, predetermined prompt to regulate response style and minimize human input bias
constraints: All test questions were multiple-choice, lacking open-ended questions
The TAQE's content and format may differ from examinations used in other countries or regions
The official TAQE website does not report category-specific human performance data, limiting GenAI-versus-human comparisons
target_learning_goals: Audiology professional knowledge across basic hearing science, behavioral audiology, electrophysiology, hearing devices, rehabilitation, and communication disorders
examples: Both models were administered all 300 questions between February 3 and February 24, 2025, with the question source concealed before testing
key_sources: Mavragani A, Hu J, Balogun Oluwadotun C, Qi B, Zheng Y, Wang Y, Xu L. (2025). Comparison of ChatGPT and DeepSeek on a Standardized Audiologist Qualification Examination in Chinese: Observational Study. JMIR Formative Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/79534

article_title: Improving clinicians' self-efficacy in delivering a diagnosis of dementia: A before-after study.
citation: FitzGerald J, Regan B, Wells Y, Bhar S, Browne W. (2025). Improving clinicians' self‐efficacy in delivering a diagnosis of dementia: A before‐after study. Australasian Journal on Ageing. https://doi.org/10.1111/ajag.70078
title: 20-item clinician self-efficacy questionnaire combining the SE-12 with eight SPIKES-D-derived items
description: A modified self-efficacy measure built by adding eight questions to the 12-item SE-12 clinical communication self-efficacy scale, covering self-efficacy in "speaking directly with the client, providing hope, involving family members in planning, coping with clients' and family members' emotions, and dealing with family dynamics". It was administered at three time points (T1, T2, T3) and total scores were summed. Internal reliability was "high (Cronbach's alpha over .92 at all three time points)", though the eight added items' validity was not tested.
requirements: Responses use the same options as the original SE-12
Total scores are calculated by summing item scores
constraints: The validity and reliability of the eight additional questions were not tested
The construct validity of the 20-item scale was not tested using factor analysis
target_learners: clinicians working in dementia memory clinics
target_learning_goals: measuring change in clinicians' self-efficacy for communicating a dementia diagnosis
examples: Administered upon study entry, one week postintervention and four months postintervention
key_sources: FitzGerald J, Regan B, Wells Y, Bhar S, Browne W. (2025). Improving clinicians' self‐efficacy in delivering a diagnosis of dementia: A before‐after study. Australasian Journal on Ageing. https://doi.org/10.1111/ajag.70078

article_title: ChatGPT's Performance on Portuguese Medical Examination Questions: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Turbo and ChatGPT-4o Mini.
citation: Filipe Prazeres. (2025). ChatGPT's Performance on Portuguese Medical Examination Questions: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Turbo and ChatGPT-4o Mini. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/65108
title: 2023 Portuguese National Examination for Access to Specialized Training (PNA) question set
description: The PNA is Portugal's examination for entry into specialized medical training, used here as a benchmark for AI performance. It includes "150 questions with 5 multiple-choice answers each, with only a single best answer", based on clinical vignettes and split into two parts of 75 questions, scored 0-150 with no penalty for blank or incorrect answers. The publicly available 2023 questions and official human candidate scores were used, with 74 non-image questions per part fed to the models in European Portuguese.
requirements: Questions must be entered in European Portuguese in a format similar to how they are presented to human candidates, with a single-letter answer requested
Each question addressed in a new chat session to reduce potential memory retention bias
constraints: Image-based questions (two, with electrocardiogram strips) cannot be answered by the text-only models and required GPT-4o
The examination has no minimum passing grade, as its purpose is ranking candidates
target_learners: Medical graduates seeking access to specialized training in Portugal
target_learning_goals: Clinical reasoning and application and integration of clinical knowledge across medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology and obstetrics, and psychiatry
examples: ChatGPT-3.5 Turbo was given part 1 (74 non-image MCQs) on July 18, 2024, and ChatGPT-4o mini part 2 (74 non-image MCQs) on July 19, 2024
key_sources: Filipe Prazeres. (2025). ChatGPT's Performance on Portuguese Medical Examination Questions: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Turbo and ChatGPT-4o Mini. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/65108

article_title: Performance of ChatGPT-4 on Taiwanese Traditional Chinese Medicine Licensing Examinations: Cross-Sectional Study.
citation: Tseng Liang-Wei, Lu Yi-Chin, Tseng Liang-Chi, Chen Yu-Chun, Chen Hsing-Yu. (2025). Performance of ChatGPT-4 on Taiwanese Traditional Chinese Medicine Licensing Examinations: Cross-Sectional Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/58897
title: 2022 Taiwanese TCM licensing examination question bank used as a GPT-4 benchmark
description: A publicly downloadable set of 480 multiple-choice questions from the first 2022 National Senior Professional and Technical Examinations for Chinese Medicine Practitioners, spanning 10 subjects across two stages, with 4 image-related questions excluded for analysis. Each domain contains 80 questions scored to 100, and "Only examinees obtaining average scores ≥60 pass the examination." The bank was characterized by cognitive level, depth of knowledge, question type, vignette style, and polarity.
requirements: Questions and answers are freely downloadable from the Taiwan Ministry of Examination after each sitting
constraints: Only the first 2022 examination was used, to mitigate prior questions being in GPT's training data; findings may not generalize to other regions or exam sittings
target_learners: TCM university students eligible for licensing examinations
target_learning_goals: TCM knowledge across basic theory, diagnosis and treatment, and clinical specialties
examples: Two TCM resident doctors took the same 476-question examination without preparation to provide human benchmark accuracy rates
key_sources: Tseng Liang-Wei, Lu Yi-Chin, Tseng Liang-Chi, Chen Yu-Chun, Chen Hsing-Yu. (2025). Performance of ChatGPT-4 on Taiwanese Traditional Chinese Medicine Licensing Examinations: Cross-Sectional Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/58897
